questions.chapter: Force: Turning Forces and Uniform Circular Motion
questions.question:
Out of the following which are examples of a couple?
1. A pair of hands turning a steering wheel
2. A man pushing a box on the floor
3. Opening a jar lid with two hands
4. A person pulling a rope tied to a well bucket
questions.solution: (a) 1 and 3. Turning a steering wheel and opening a jar lid with two hands involve two equal, opposite, parallel forces not in the same line (a couple); pushing a box and pulling a rope are single forces. (Options c and d are printed identically.)

questions.question: A machine converts 800 J of electric energy to 600 J of mechanical energy. Its efficiency is:
questions.solution: (b) 75%. Efficiency = output/input × 100 = 600/800 × 100 = 75%.

questions.question: Look at the diagram and name the type of lever. [Diagram: a broom]
questions.solution: (c) Class 3. When sweeping, the upper hand acts as the fulcrum, the lower hand applies the effort between fulcrum and load, and the load (friction of dust) acts at the bristles.
questions.figure_desc: Picture of a sweeping broom (long handle with bristles at the bottom).

questions.topic: Refraction from denser to rarer medium
questions.question: When light passes from denser to rarer medium, which statement is incorrect?

options.a: The angle of refraction is greater than the angle of incidence.

questions.solution: (c) The wavelength decreases. Going into a rarer medium the speed increases and frequency stays constant, so the wavelength increases (λ = v/f).

questions.question: Which of the following is not an application of a concave lens?
questions.solution: (d) Magnifying glass. A magnifying glass is a convex lens; concave lenses are used for myopia correction, peepholes and wide-angle lenses.

questions.question: Which property of electromagnetic waves determine whether they are classified as radio waves, visible light or X rays?
questions.solution: (c) Wavelength. All EM waves travel at the same speed in vacuum; they are classified by wavelength (or frequency).

questions.question:
A man is standing between two high hills as shown in the diagram (man M between hill H1 at distance x and hill H2 at distance y).
The man fires a shot and hears two echoes. If the first echo is heard 1 second after firing and second echo is heard 2 second after firing. What is the distance between two hills? (Speed of sound = 340 m/s)
If three resistors R1, R2 and R3 are connected in series with a supply. What is the relation between current drawn by each of them if R1 > R2 > R3.
questions.solution: (a) I1 = I2 = I3. In series the same current flows through every resistor.

questions.question: After a power surge, which protection device would allow you to restore power most quickly?
questions.solution: (c) An MCB. It trips on overload and can simply be reset by pushing the switch back, without replacing any wire.

questions.topic: Magnetic field at centre of circular loop
questions.question: In a circular loop carrying current, the magnetic field at the centre of the loop is:

options.a: Parallel to the plane of the loop
options.b: Perpendicular to the plane of the loop
options.c: At an angle 45° to the plane of the loop

questions.solution: (b) Perpendicular to the plane of the loop.

questions.question: If two bodies have the same thermal capacity but different masses, they must have:
questions.solution: (b) Different specific heats. Heat capacity C = mc; same C with different m requires different c.

questions.question: If Uranium-238 emits an alpha particle, the resulting element will be:
questions.solution: (a) Thorium-234. ²³⁸₉₂U → ²³⁴₉₀Th + ⁴₂He (mass number −4, atomic number −2).

questions.question:
Assertion(A): The frequency of alternating current in Indian households is 50 Hz.
Reason(R): AC in India changes its direction every 0.01 s

options.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, R is false
options.d: R is true, A is false

questions.solution: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A. AC reverses direction twice per cycle; reversal every 0.01 s means a period of 0.02 s, i.e. f = 1/0.02 = 50 Hz.

questions.question:
Assertion(A): A large body always has a higher temperature than the small one.
Reason(R): Temperature depends on the average kinetic energy of molecules

options.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, R is false
options.d: R is true, A is false

questions.solution: (d) R is true, A is false. Temperature depends on the average kinetic energy of molecules, not on the size of the body; a large body may hold more heat but need not be hotter.

questions.question:
Assertion(A): Dolphins can detect the presence of fish using echolocation
Reason(R): Dolphin produce low frequency sounds to identify obstacles

options.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, R is false
options.d: R is true, A is false

questions.solution: (c) A is true, R is false. Dolphins use high-frequency ultrasonic sound (not low frequency) for echolocation.

questions.question: State two differences between absolute and relative refractive index
questions.solution:
1. Absolute RI is the RI of a medium with respect to vacuum (n = c/v), whereas relative RI is the RI of one medium with respect to another medium (₁n₂ = v₁/v₂).
2. Absolute RI is always greater than 1, whereas relative RI may be greater than, less than or equal to 1.

marking_points.point: Definition difference: w.r.t. vacuum vs w.r.t. another medium
Absolute RI always > 1; relative RI can be < 1, = 1 or > 1

questions.question: A block and tackle system has 3 pulleys in each block. If an effort of 100 N (effort applied in downward direction) is required to raise a load of 480 N, calculate the efficiency of the system.
questions.solution: Total pulleys n = 6, so V.R. = 6. M.A. = L/E = 480/100 = 4.8. Efficiency η = M.A./V.R. × 100 = 4.8/6 × 100 = 80%.

questions.chapter: Force: Turning Forces and Uniform Circular Motion
questions.topic: Centre of gravity of conical pot
questions.question:
Paresh took an earthen pot which was filled with water up to its brim. The earthen pot was conical in shape and kept with its apex in downward direction.
a) If the vertical height of the earthen pot is 12 cm, where does its centre of gravity lie?
b) Paresh poured out all the water from the pot. How will its centre of gravity shift: Towards the open end or Towards the apex?
questions.solution:
(a) A cone filled completely behaves like a solid cone; its C.G. lies on the axis at h/4 from the base (open end), i.e. 12/4 = 3 cm below the open end (9 cm above the apex).
(b) Towards the apex. The empty pot is a hollow conical shell whose C.G. lies at h/3 = 4 cm from the open end (8 cm above the apex), so the C.G. shifts towards the apex.

marking_points.point: (a) On the axis, h/4 = 3 cm from the open end (9 cm from apex)

questions.question:
State the dependence of angle of deviation in prism on:
a) RI of material of prism
b) wavelength of light
questions.solution:
(a) The greater the refractive index of the material of the prism, the greater the angle of deviation.
(b) The greater the wavelength of light, the smaller the angle of deviation (red deviates least, violet most).

marking_points.point: (a) Deviation increases with increase in RI
(b) Deviation decreases with increase in wavelength

questions.question: We are able to see TV channels clearly when we set the TV on auto tuning. State and define the phenomena responsible for this.
questions.solution: Resonance. When the frequency of the receiver (tuning) circuit is adjusted to become equal to the frequency of the transmitted signal, it picks up that signal with maximum amplitude. Resonance is the phenomenon in which a body vibrates with a large amplitude when the frequency of the externally applied periodic force equals its natural frequency.

marking_points.point: Definition: large-amplitude vibration when applied frequency equals natural frequency

questions.question: State any two advantages of parallel combination in household circuits
questions.solution:
1. Each appliance gets the same (full mains) voltage of 220 V.
2. Each appliance can be switched on or off independently; if one appliance fails, the others keep working.

marking_points.point: Independent switching / failure of one does not affect others

concepts: effect of pressure on boiling point
questions.question: Rishi is surprised to see water boiling at 115°C. Give reason to why water can boil at the above temperature?
questions.solution: The boiling point of water rises above 100 °C when the pressure on its surface is increased (e.g. inside a pressure cooker) or when impurities such as salt are dissolved in it. Hence water under increased pressure (or containing dissolved impurities) can boil at 115 °C.

marking_points.point: Boiling point increases with increase in pressure
So water under higher pressure (pressure cooker)/with dissolved impurities boils at 115 °C

questions.topic: Pitch and frequency from wave graph
questions.question: The figure shows two waves of different frequencies. Which one of them is a shrill note? State the reason?
questions.solution: Wave (a) is the shrill note. It has a shorter wavelength, i.e. more oscillations in the same time, so its frequency is higher; pitch (shrillness) increases with frequency.

marking_points.point: Higher frequency (more waves in the same time) means higher pitch

questions.figure_desc: Two displacement-time graphs: (a) many closely spaced waves of small wavelength λ; (b) fewer, widely spaced waves of larger wavelength λ'.

questions.question: Three resistors of value 2 ohm, 3 ohm and 6 ohm are connected parallel to a cell of emf 2 V. Find the value of current drawn by the circuit if the internal resistance of the cell is 1 ohm.
questions.solution: 1/Rp = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 1, so Rp = 1 Ω. Total resistance = Rp + r = 1 + 1 = 2 Ω. I = ε/(R + r) = 2/2 = 1 A.

marking_points.point: Total resistance 2 Ω including internal resistance

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
[Figure: a coil of insulated wire wound on an iron nail, connected to a battery; − terminal on the tip side, + terminal on the head side.]
Figure shows an electromagnet. State the polarity developed on the tip of the nail. State any two ways to decrease the strength of the magnetic field produced.
questions.solution:
Polarity: South pole at the tip. Current enters from the + terminal at the head end and leaves at the tip end; seen from the tip, the current in the turns flows clockwise, so the tip becomes a South pole (clock rule).
Ways to decrease strength: (1) decrease the current (use fewer cells / add resistance), (2) decrease the number of turns of the coil (or remove the soft-iron nail core).

marking_points.point: Tip of nail: South pole (clock rule)
Decrease number of turns / remove iron core

questions.figure_desc: Iron nail wound with a coil of insulated wire; the coil ends are connected to a battery with − on the nail-tip side and + on the head side.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Figure shows the socket used for electric connection (a three-pin socket: terminal 1 is the large top hole, terminals 2 and 3 are the two smaller lower holes on the left and right).
a) State the colour code of wire to be used for second terminal
b) What is the use of third terminal
c) Why is the first terminal made thicker than others?
questions.solution:
(a) Terminal 2 (lower left) is the neutral terminal: wire colour light blue (old code: black).
(b) Terminal 3 (lower right) is the live terminal: it connects the live wire and supplies current at high potential to the appliance (the switch and fuse are in this line).
(c) Terminal 1 is the earth terminal; it is made thicker (and the earth pin longer) so that the plug cannot be inserted the wrong way and the earth connection, having low resistance, is made first, ensuring safety against shocks.

marking_points.point: (b) Live terminal – brings current to appliance
(c) Earth terminal is thicker: low resistance, cannot be inserted wrongly / makes earth connection first

questions.figure_desc: Front view of a three-pin socket: hole 1 (large) at the top, holes 2 (left) and 3 (right) smaller at the bottom.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Parallel circuit: find R and branch current
questions.question:
Find the value of R in the following circuit. Also find value of current in ammeter 1.
Circuit: a 12 V battery; ammeter A2 in the main line reads 5.0 A; the circuit then divides into two parallel branches – one containing ammeter A1 in series with a 3.0 Ω resistor, the other containing resistor R.
questions.solution:
The battery (negligible internal resistance) applies 12 V across each parallel branch.
Current in A1 = V/R = 12/3 = 4 A.
Current through R = 5.0 − 4 = 1 A.
R = 12/1 = 12 Ω.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: State three differences between nuclear fusion and nuclear fission.
questions.solution:
1. Fission: a heavy nucleus splits into two lighter nuclei; fusion: two light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus.
2. Fission can occur at ordinary temperature (needs slow neutrons); fusion needs extremely high temperature (~10⁷ K) and pressure.
3. Fission products are radioactive (nuclear waste); fusion products are generally not radioactive. (Also: energy per unit mass is greater in fusion; fission can be controlled in reactors, fusion is not yet controllable.)

marking_points.point: Splitting of heavy nucleus vs combining of light nuclei
Conditions: ordinary temperature/neutron bombardment vs very high temperature and pressure
Radioactive waste vs no radioactive waste (or energy per unit mass / controllability)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
An atomic nucleus A is composed of 84 protons and 128 neutrons.
a) Nucleus A emits an alpha particle to become B. What is the composition of B?
b) Nucleus B emits the beta particle and is transformed to C. What is the composition of C?
c) Does the composition of nucleus C change if it emits gamma radiation?
questions.solution:
A: Z = 84, N = 128 (mass number 212).
(a) Alpha emission: Z − 2, N − 2 → B has 82 protons and 126 neutrons (mass number 208).
(b) Beta emission: one neutron changes into a proton → C has 83 protons and 125 neutrons (mass number 208).
(c) No. Gamma emission only releases energy; the numbers of protons and neutrons remain the same.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Frequency of stretched string and wave speed
questions.question:
a) A wire of length 80 cm has a frequency of 256 Hz. Calculate the length of similar wire under similar tension which will have frequency 1024 Hz.
b) A certain sound has a frequency of 256 Hz and wavelength of 1.3 m. Calculate the speed of this wave.
questions.solution:
(a) For the same wire and tension, f ∝ 1/l, so f₁l₁ = f₂l₂ → l₂ = 256 × 80/1024 = 20 cm.
(b) v = fλ = 256 × 1.3 = 332.8 m/s.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: A virtual diminished image is formed between the optical centre and the principal focus of the lens. Name the type of lens. Draw a neat and labelled diagram to show the position of object and image.
questions.solution:
Concave (diverging) lens.
Diagram: object AB placed anywhere in front of the concave lens (e.g. beyond F). A ray from B parallel to the principal axis diverges after refraction so that it appears to come from the focus F₁ on the object side (dotted backward extension). A ray from B through optical centre O goes undeviated. The dotted extension and this ray meet at B'; A'B' is drawn between O and F₁ on the same side as the object: virtual, erect and diminished. Label O, F₁, F₂, AB, A'B' and arrows on rays.

marking_points.point: Correct ray diagram with two rays and dotted extensions
Image A'B' between O and F, virtual, erect, diminished; labels

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
The spreading of light by the air molecules is called the scattering of light. The light having the least wavelength scatters more. The sun appears red at sunrise and sunset. The appearance of blue sky is due to scattering of light. The colour of the scattered light depends on the size of particles. The smaller molecules in the atmosphere scatter smaller wavelengths of light. The amount of scattering of light depends on the wavelength of light. When light from the sun enters the earth's atmosphere it gets scattered by the dust particles and air molecules present in the atmosphere. The path of sunlight entering the dark room through a fine hole is seen because of scattering of sunlight by dust particles present in its path inside the room.
Answer the following questions.
a) Why do astronauts in spaceships observe that the colour of earth appears blue?
b) Why are danger signals made in red colour?
c) The smoke from a fire looks white, give reason.
questions.solution:
(a) Blue light (short wavelength) from sunlight is scattered the most by air molecules of the earth's atmosphere (scattering ∝ 1/λ⁴); this scattered blue light (along with light from the oceans) reaches the astronauts, so the earth appears blue.
(b) Red light has the longest wavelength in the visible spectrum, so it is scattered the least and can travel the farthest through air, fog and smoke; hence it is visible from a large distance.
(c) Smoke contains large particles (larger than the wavelength of light) which scatter all wavelengths almost equally; the mixture of all scattered colours appears white.

marking_points.point: (a) Blue scattered most by atmosphere reaches the observer
(c) Large particles scatter all colours equally → white

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Speed of light and RI across three media
questions.question:
The wavelength of light becomes half when it moves from medium 1 to medium 2 in the following diagram. And the speed of light increases to three times when it moves from medium 2 to 3. If medium 3 is vacuum, find the speed of light in medium 1. Hence find RI of medium 1 with respect to medium 3.
(Diagram: a ray passes from medium 1 (n₁) into medium 2 (n₂) and then into medium 3 (n₃), arranged as three horizontal layers.)
questions.solution:
Medium 3 is vacuum: v₃ = c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s.
v₃ = 3v₂ → v₂ = 1 × 10⁸ m/s.
Frequency is unchanged, so v ∝ λ; λ₂ = λ₁/2 → v₂ = v₁/2 → v₁ = 2 × 10⁸ m/s.
RI of medium 1 w.r.t. medium 3 (vacuum) = v₃/v₁ = 3 × 10⁸/2 × 10⁸ = 1.5.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.chapter: Force: Turning Forces and Uniform Circular Motion
questions.topic: Balancing a metre rule to find its mass
questions.question: A uniform meter rule is balanced horizontally at the 60 cm mark by suspending 10 gf at one end. Draw the arrangement for the same and find the mass of the rule.
questions.solution:
Diagram: metre rule on a knife edge (fulcrum) at 60 cm, 10 gf hung at the 100 cm end, weight W of the rule acting downward at its C.G. (50 cm mark).
Taking moments about the fulcrum: W × (60 − 50) = 10 × (100 − 60) → W × 10 = 400 → W = 40 gf. Mass of the rule = 40 g.

marking_points.point: Diagram: fulcrum at 60 cm, 10 gf at 100 cm, W at 50 cm

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Work done while holding a load
questions.question:
An old man was standing on a bus stand carrying very heavy luggage. Ravi was looking at the old man and finding him uncomfortable. He requested him to put down the luggage and help him do so.
a) did the old man do any work while holding the luggage?
b) write the equation for work done against gravity.
c) Is work done against gravity positive or negative?
questions.solution:
(a) No. While merely holding the luggage there is no displacement, so W = F × s = 0 (though he gets tired due to muscular effort).
(b) W = mgh (m = mass, g = acceleration due to gravity, h = vertical height).
(c) Work done against gravity (by the applied force) is positive, since the applied force and displacement are in the same direction; the work done by gravity itself is negative.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
A man uses a crowbar of length 150 cm to raise a load of 75 kgf by putting the sharp edge below the bar at a distance of 1 m from his hand.
a) Draw a diagram of arrangement showing fulcrum load and effort with their directions
b) identify the kind of lever in a crowbar.
c) calculate the mechanical advantage and the effort needed.
questions.solution:
(a) Diagram: crowbar resting on a fulcrum (stone/sharp edge) 1 m from the effort end; effort E applied downward at the hand end; load L (75 kgf) at the other end acting downward on the bar, 50 cm from the fulcrum.
(b) Class I lever (fulcrum between load and effort).
(c) Effort arm = 100 cm, load arm = 150 − 100 = 50 cm. M.A. = effort arm/load arm = 100/50 = 2. Effort = L/M.A. = 75/2 = 37.5 kgf.

marking_points.point: Diagram with F, L, E and directions

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Latent heat of fusion; cold after hailstorm
concepts: cooling due to melting of ice
questions.question:
a) Define latent heat of fusion.
b) Why does it become colder after hailstorm, than before or during the hailstorm?
questions.solution:
(a) Specific latent heat of fusion is the amount of heat energy required to convert unit mass of a solid into liquid at its melting point without any change in temperature.
(b) After the hailstorm the hailstones (ice) melt. For melting, each gram of ice absorbs 336 J of latent heat from the surroundings, so the temperature of the surroundings falls and it becomes colder.

marking_points.point: (a) Correct definition with 'no change in temperature'
(b) Absorb latent heat from surroundings, so surroundings cool

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
The above graph shows the heating curve for sodium chloride. (Temperature (°C) vs time: A at 0 °C rising steeply to B at 801 °C; flat BC at 801 °C; CD rising less steeply to D at 1465 °C; flat DE at 1465 °C.)
a) Which part of the graph shows melting of sodium chloride?
b) What is the boiling point of sodium chloride?
c) Why is the slope of part AB more than the slope of part CD?
questions.solution:
(a) BC (temperature constant at 801 °C while the solid melts).
(b) 1465 °C (part DE).
(c) AB shows heating of solid NaCl and CD of liquid NaCl. With the same rate of heat supply, rise of temperature per unit time is inversely proportional to specific heat capacity; the solid has a lower specific heat capacity than the liquid, so its temperature rises faster and AB is steeper.

marking_points.point: (c) Solid has lower specific heat capacity than liquid, so faster temperature rise

questions.figure_desc: Heating curve for sodium chloride: temperature vs time with points A (0 °C), B and C at 801 °C, D and E at 1465 °C.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: A household has a fuse of 5 A rating. Calculate the maximum number of bulbs of rating 55 W, 220 V each that can be connected in the circuit. Also find the resistance of each bulb.
questions.solution:
Current drawn by each bulb I = P/V = 55/220 = 0.25 A. Maximum number of bulbs = 5/0.25 = 20 (equivalently, maximum power = 220 × 5 = 1100 W; 1100/55 = 20).
Resistance of each bulb R = V²/P = 220 × 220/55 = 880 Ω.

marking_points.point: I per bulb = 0.25 A (or P max = 1100 W)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
a) Is it possible for a hydrogen nucleus to emit an Alpha particle? Give a reason for your answer.
b) Define isotopes.
questions.solution:
(a) No. An alpha particle consists of 2 protons and 2 neutrons, but a hydrogen nucleus has only one proton (and no neutron), so it cannot emit an alpha particle.
(b) Isotopes are atoms of the same element having the same atomic number but different mass numbers (i.e. different numbers of neutrons), e.g. ¹H, ²H, ³H.

marking_points.point: (a) Reason: hydrogen nucleus has only one proton; alpha needs 2p + 2n

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Energy loss on a slope: momentum and height
concepts: conservation of energy with friction loss
questions.question:
Richa skates from the top of the slope, and gains a speed of 15 m/s. She loses 25 % of energy to friction.
a) If mass of Richa is 50 kg, find her momentum when she reaches bottom of the slope.
b) What is the height of the slope? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution:
(a) p = mv = 50 × 15 = 750 kg m/s.
(b) KE at bottom = ½mv² = ½ × 50 × 15² = 5625 J. This is 75% of the initial potential energy: 0.75 × mgh = 5625 → mgh = 7500 J → h = 7500/(50 × 10) = 15 m.

audit_excluded.reason: Part (a) polarity depends on the winding sense, which the low-resolution clip-art figure does not show clearly (horizontal front strands, no current arrows). The most plausible reading (wire enters top-right, passes behind, front strands carry current left to right, anticlockwise seen from above) gives a North pole at the top, contradicting the stored South; the stored answer itself admits it depends on the drawing.
